- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.50) and price is trending up, model frequently overfits upward momentum; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.50); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lagged correction.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.80 to 0.00), model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days and reduce by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
